title: War between Israel, the US and Iran

charter.in: The war between Israel and the United States on one side and Iran on the other that began with the US-Israeli strikes on Iran of 28 February 2026: Israeli and US strikes on Iran, Iran's missile and drone strikes on Israel, on US forces and on the Gulf states, the deaths and damage they cause, the killing of Iran's leaders, threats and decisions to widen, pause or resume the strikes, and the ceasefires, deals and talks to end the war. A story belongs when that war is its main subject.
out: The Israel–Hezbollah war in and over Lebanon

Disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz: closures and reopenings, attacks on or seizures of merchant ships, stranded ships, insurance, escorts, blockades of the strait's traffic, tolls and passage terms
Houthi attacks, the Red Sea and the war in Yemen
Iran's nuclear program, enriched uranium, inspections and nuclear talks, except as terms in talks to end the war
Oil, gas and fuel prices and markets; energy, fertilizer and food shortages in importing countries
The pre-war standoff, military buildup and nuclear talks before 28 February 2026
Iran's internal politics, protests and crackdowns not caused by the war
US sanctions on Iran and the US land blockade ('Iron Gate')
Gaza, the West Bank and Syria
charter.endEvent: A lasting end to the fighting between Israel/the US and Iran: strikes on Iran and Iran's strikes on Israel, US forces and the Gulf states stop under a ceasefire or deal that our later stories do not show broken by renewed strikes. A truce later broken does not count.

figures.name: Deaths in Iran
figures.definition: People killed in Iran by the US and Israeli strikes since 28 February 2026, civilians and military, all of Iran, by whichever source our story cites (Iranian officials, the Red Crescent, HRANA). Cumulative. Not deaths in Lebanon, Israel, Iraq or the Gulf states, and not the crew of the frigate Dena sunk off Sri Lanka.
variants: civilians only (e.g. "at least 1,332 Iranian civilians", UN experts' "about 1,000 civilian deaths")
a war toll with no stated place, which may include Lebanon (e.g. "has killed over 2,000 people")
one strike round or one strike only (e.g. "US strikes previously killed 14 people")
all war dead on every front ("more than 7,000 dead")

figures.name: US service members killed
figures.definition: US service members killed in the war since 28 February 2026, by Iranian or Iran-aligned attacks anywhere in the region. Cumulative.
variants: one strike only (e.g. three soldiers killed at a Jordanian air base)

entries.title: US and Israel launch strikes on Iran; missiles fired back
entries.why: Start of the war: the US-Israeli strikes of 28 February and Iran's missiles fired back at Israel.

entries.title: US and Israeli strikes kill over 200 in Iran

values.quote: killed at least 201 people and wounded 747

entries.why: First death toll of the opening strikes and Iran's retaliation on Israel and US bases; same event as the launch story.

entries.title: Israeli and US strikes coincide with mass online shutdown
entries.why: Mainly the internet blackout and censorship inside Iran ("the event mainly changes internal information flow and repression tactics"), with the opening strikes and cyberattacks as its setting: the cyber angle.

entries.title: US and Israel attack Iran; Tehran launches missile strikes

values.countedAs: deaths in one strike (the Minab school) only
values.quote: a school in Minab that killed at least 51

entries.why: Maps the opening strikes (ministries, the Minab school) and Iran's missile and drone waves; repeats the opening event.

entries.title: Israel strikes Tehran after Khamenei killing; Iran retaliates
entries.why: Khamenei's killing and heavy strikes on Tehran with Iranian barrages; the Hormuz closure is a side strand (a Hormuz near miss).

entries.title: Khamenei killed, Iran's leaders scramble amid war threats
entries.why: The succession crisis after Khamenei's killing; same event and day as the turning point.

entries.title: Blasts hit Dubai and Doha, key hubs damaged
entries.why: Iran widens its retaliation from US bases to Gulf cities' airports, hotels and ports: a new target set.

entries.title: Missiles overwhelm Israel's defenses, at least ten killed
entries.why: Iranian salvos kill at least ten in Israel (nine in Bet Shemesh); a heavy round of the retaliation already reported.

entries.title: Trump says fighting could last a month after heavy strikes
entries.why: Trump's month-long campaign statement, the strike tally and the first US casualties.

entries.title: Starmer allows US to use UK bases against Iran
entries.why: An ally's decision to support the US campaign.

entries.title: Leaders urged to avoid steps that could provoke Iran
entries.why: Saudi push for Gulf restraint after the strikes: the Gulf states' decisions about the war.

entries.title: Heavy Israeli strikes hit Tehran broadcaster and prison
entries.why: A further Israeli strike round on Tehran's state targets.

entries.title: US and Israel strike Iran as counterstrikes spread
entries.why: Continued strikes framed as regime change and Iranian counterstrikes in several countries.

entries.title: U.S. interceptors deplete, risking Pacific readiness
entries.why: Mainly US interceptor stocks and Pacific readiness: munitions drained by the war, as in the optional arms-depletion story of 3 May.

entries.title: US risks running out of missile defenses in Iran conflict
entries.why: Mainly interceptor stocks against Iran's barrages: munitions drained by the war; same theme as the day's other depletion story.

entries.title: Israel and US strike Iran as region teeters toward war

values.countedAs: people killed in Tehran and Beirut together (includes Lebanon)

entries.why: Strikes on Tehran and Iran's broadcaster and Trump's four-week campaign; Beirut and Hormuz are side strands (a Lebanon near miss).

entries.title: US, Israel strike Iran; Dubai embassy hit, oil disrupted

values.countedAs: war dead with no stated place; the story covers strikes on Iran and Lebanon
values.quote: including strikes on Qom and at least 787 dead

entries.why: Strikes on Qom, the death toll and an Iranian hit on the US embassy in Dubai.

entries.title: US and Israeli strikes hit Qom assembly building
entries.why: A strike on the body choosing Khamenei's successor; part of the leadership strand.

entries.title: Iran hits Arab states and US bases, damaging energy sites
entries.why: Iranian strikes on Gulf states, energy sites and US bases; follows the Gulf turning points.

entries.title: Trump team seeks congressional backing for Iran strikes
entries.why: The administration briefs Congress on the war ahead of war-powers votes.

entries.title: France sends flagship to Mediterranean amid Iran strikes
entries.why: A French carrier deployment in response to the war: an ally's decision.

entries.title: Russia suspends work after losing contact with Iran’s atomic leaders
entries.why: Rosatom halts work at Bushehr because of the fighting: war harm, but its nuclear-facility framing borders on the nuclear exclusion.

entries.title: US sinks Iranian ship, NATO downs missile toward Türkiye
entries.why: The war reaches the Indian Ocean and NATO: a US submarine sinks an Iranian warship and NATO downs a missile aimed at Türkiye.

entries.title: US and Israel hit Iran; attacks spark strikes, oil shock

values.countedAs: schoolgirls killed in one strike (the Minab school) only

entries.why: Roundup of strikes, Iranian retaliation and casualties; the oil shock is secondary.

entries.title: US adds B-52s and reports nearly 2,000 targets hit
entries.why: The US adds B-52s and reports its target tally; the Hormuz closure is a side strand.

entries.title: Senate fails to rein in Trump's Iran strikes
entries.why: The Senate rejects a war-powers resolution 47-52: a decision by Congress about the war that keeps the status quo.

entries.title: Fact-finding mission says US, Israel violated Iran's sovereignty
entries.why: A UN probe finds the strikes and Iran's reprisals breached the UN Charter, with child deaths from the war; the detainee strand is secondary.

entries.title: US to raze Iran's ballistic weapons plants
entries.why: The US announces a next phase, from launchers to Iran's missile industry, with ground options not ruled out: a new target set.

entries.title: US and Israel intensify strikes on Tehran sites

values.quote: Iranian officials report at least 1,230 dead

entries.why: Sixth day of strikes on Iran, the civilian toll and attacks on health facilities.

entries.title: House rejects bid to halt Trump's Iran war
entries.why: The House rejects a war-powers resolution 219-212; same strand as the Senate vote.

entries.title: U.S. strikes topple Iran government, demand unconditional surrender
entries.why: The air campaign that killed Iran's leaders and the US demand for unconditional surrender; the killings were reported on 1-2 March.

entries.title: US and Israel strikes kill over 1,200, rattle markets
entries.why: The death toll, Trump's "unconditional surrender" demand and a 4-6 week timeline; markets are secondary.

entries.title: President vows to confront threats amid Iran strikes
entries.why: Continued Iranian strikes on the UAE (airports, a US consulate, desalination) and the UAE's response.

entries.title: Israel uses AI to guide strikes on Iran
entries.why: About military AI targeting, with the strikes on Iran and their civilian toll as its case: a split subject.

entries.title: Mojtaba Khamenei named Iran's new leader after strikes
entries.why: First story on the hardline successor named after the strikes killed his father, with new Israeli and US threats against successors.

entries.title: US, Israel bomb Iranian sites; toxic rain, 35% oil price spike
entries.why: First story on strikes on Tehran's fuel depots, a new civilian-energy target set, with toxic rain over the city.

entries.title: Trump rejects talks, suggests killing Iran's leaders

values.countedAs: Iranian civilians reported killed only
values.quote: at least 1,332 Iranian civilians were reported killed

entries.why: Trump's war aims (no talks, destroying the military and leaders); restates the surrender line of the day before.

entries.title: Dubai airport briefly closed after missile and drone barrage
entries.why: Iran's strikes on the Gulf states (Dubai, Doha, Bahrain); those strikes began in the first days.

entries.title: Trump says Iran campaign 'very soon' as oil tops $100
entries.why: Leads on the US strike campaign and Trump's claims about its gains and length; Lebanon and oil are background (a Lebanon near miss).

entries.title: Trump says he's 'not happy' after Tehran names Khamenei's son

values.countedAs: the regional war's toll with no stated place; may include Lebanon

entries.why: Trump's reaction to Mojtaba Khamenei's appointment reported the day before.

entries.title: U.S. submarine sank Iranian frigate; 104 reported dead
entries.why: The frigate Dena's sinking, first reported on 5 March; updates the crew toll.

entries.title: Iran escalates missile and energy attacks to wear down foes
entries.why: Analysis of Iran's war strategy: IRGC control and an attrition campaign of missiles and drones.

entries.title: Saudi warns Iran, threatens retaliation and US base use
entries.why: Riyadh threatens to retaliate or open its bases to the US after Iranian strikes, and Iran's president apologizes to neighbors: the war's Gulf front.

entries.title: Revolutionary Guards install new supreme leader, stir regional tensions
entries.why: The IRGC's role in the wartime succession and what it means for the war; follows the 9 March appointment.

entries.title: Senator says US may send forces into Iran

values.quote: at least 150 U.S. troops wounded and eight killed

entries.why: A possible widening to ground forces, US casualties and the fight over authorization; a senator's reading, not a decision.

entries.title: Mojtaba Khamenei named Iran's top authority
entries.why: The succession follows the war's killing of Khamenei, but this explainer frames it as domestic politics and never mentions the war.

entries.title: US estimates $11.3 billion cost after six-day Iran campaign

values.countedAs: war toll with no stated place (the conflict "spread regionally"); may include Lebanon

entries.why: First official figure for what the war costs the US, with depleted munitions and a coming funding request.

entries.title: Senate Democrats demand probe after girls' deaths

values.countedAs: civilians killed over the campaign, Iran's claim given as a range (hundreds to over a thousand)
values.quote: killed hundreds to over a thousand civilians

entries.why: Civilian deaths from the 28 February strikes, likely US responsibility for them, and congressional oversight of the war.

entries.title: Israel strikes spark toxic black rain over Tehran
entries.why: Health and environmental harm in Tehran from the depot strikes first reported on 9 March.

entries.title: Iran-linked hackers hit major device maker
entries.why: A cyberattack framed as retaliation for a deadly strike in Iran opens a cyber front, but the story is mostly one company's outage.

entries.title: US sends thousands of Marines to Middle East after attacks
entries.why: Prompted by ship attacks near Hormuz, but it reports a war buildup that could become a ground operation (Kharg Island): split with shipping.

entries.title: Israel and US expand attacks after cross-border rocket fire
entries.why: A regional photo roundup led by Beirut; US bombers flying from UK bases against Iran are one strand of several.

entries.title: Trump urges allies to keep Strait open amid strikes

values.countedAs: deaths in one round of strikes on Isfahan province only

entries.why: Splits its subject between US-Israeli strikes on Isfahan and Trump's call to keep Hormuz open.

entries.title: Trump rejects mediation, orders continued strikes in Iran

values.countedAs: the conflict's toll with no stated place; may include Lebanon

entries.why: Washington turns down mediators' ceasefire overtures and Iran refuses a ceasefire while strikes go on; repeats the no-talks stance reported on 9 March.

entries.title: Zelensky accuses Russia of aiding Iran attacks
entries.why: Russian drones and intelligence for Iran's strikes on US and regional bases, but told from Ukraine's side and its own war: outside support, as in the October China-Russia piece.

entries.title: U.S. shifts missiles and ships to Middle East, allies worry
entries.why: Missile defenses and ships moved from the Indo-Pacific for the war, but mainly about allies' deterrence worries and strained munitions stocks, as in the 3 March interceptor stories.

entries.title: Millions flee as regional war widens
entries.why: A humanitarian roundup in which displacement inside Iran from the campaign is one strand next to Lebanon, Gaza and Sudan.

entries.title: Israel warns of thousands more targets in Iran
entries.why: Led by the Israel-Iran exchanges, Israel's warning of thousands more targets and strikes on bases hosting US forces; Lebanon and Hormuz are secondary (a Lebanon near miss).

entries.title: Top hardline coordinator killed in Israeli strike
entries.why: Israel kills Ali Larijani, Iran's security coordinator and an interlocutor in talks: another senior leader removed.

entries.title: US, Israel strikes widen conflict across nearly a dozen states

values.countedAs: civilian deaths in Iran only (independent UN experts)
children killed in one airstrike on the Minab school only

entries.why: UN experts on deaths, displacement and damage inside Iran from the strikes, and the war's spread.

entries.title: Iran strikes Qatar hub, missiles hit Saudi targets
entries.why: After Iran's Pars gas field is hit, Iran strikes Qatar's Ras Laffan and Saudi Arabia: a tit-for-tat round against energy sites.

entries.title: U.S. weighs thousands of troops for Strait and oil missions
entries.why: A possible US ground deployment, split between Hormuz and oil missions (the strait, Kharg Island) and securing uranium.

entries.title: Iran strikes Tel Aviv with cluster missiles
entries.why: Iran's retaliatory missile strikes on Israel and Israeli strikes on Iran; Lebanon is background (a Lebanon near miss).

entries.title: Trump urges Israel not to hit Iranian gas facilities
entries.why: The US tells Israel not to repeat strikes on Iranian energy sites after Ras Laffan: a first restraint on how the war is fought, and a US-Israel split.

entries.title: Strikes, leadership assassination push Iran conflict toward wider war
entries.why: Analysis of the war's escalation (assassinations, deep strikes, a House vote leaving the president free to act).

entries.title: US approves $16.5bn sale to UAE, Kuwait and Jordan
entries.why: An emergency arms sale to Gulf allies justified by the war; the subject is the arms transfer and Congress being bypassed.

entries.title: Iran warns 'zero restraint' after strikes cut Qatar LNG 17%
entries.why: Iran's threat of "zero restraint" and the Ras Laffan damage from the energy round first reported on 19 March.

entries.title: Israel launches fresh strikes on Iran
entries.why: New Israeli strikes on Iran, Iranian counterattacks on Gulf states and allies split over joining in.

entries.title: Iran missiles hit southern Israel, more than 100 injured
entries.why: Iran's fiercest attack on Israel so far hits near the Dimona nuclear site after Natanz was struck.

entries.title: Trump threatens to obliterate Iran power plants

values.quote: killed more than 2,000 people in Iran

entries.why: Trump threatens to destroy Iran's power plants, a new civilian target set, and Iran fires 4,000-km missiles; reopening Hormuz is the ultimatum's condition (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: Pakistan rushes to avert Iran‑Saudi direct war
entries.why: Mediation to keep Iran's strikes on the Gulf from becoming an Iran-Saudi war.

entries.title: US issues 48-hour ultimatum to Iran over Hormuz
entries.why: Mass Iranian missile launches, Israeli strikes on Tehran and damage to water and power; follows the 22 March ultimatum, with Hormuz its condition.

entries.title: US threatens Iran power plants after waterway blockade
entries.why: The power-plant threat, Iran's counter-threats against US energy and desalination, and missiles near Dimona; the blockade is background.

entries.title: Democrats demand hearings after missiles target Israel and Diego Garcia
entries.why: Iranian missiles at southern Israel and toward Diego Garcia, and the fight in Congress over oversight of the war.

entries.title: Trump’s threats and mixed messages raise regional conflict risks
entries.why: Where the war stands in week four: Iran surviving its leadership losses, its strikes, and Trump's contradictory threats.

entries.title: US says it sent 15-point proposal to Iran
entries.why: The first concrete US offer to settle the war.

entries.title: Iran fires missiles at Israel, energy trade hit
entries.why: Leads with the direct Iran-Israel missile and air exchange (Tel Aviv damage, Tehran command centers hit); Hormuz and markets are secondary.

entries.title: Baghdad summons US and Iranian envoys after deadly strikes
entries.why: Mainly Iraq's diplomatic response, but the strikes on the PMF and a Kurdish headquarters are the war spilling into Iraq.

entries.title: White House says goals met in two weeks despite lawmakers
entries.why: US war aims and timeline (two more weeks, leadership change) and pushback in Congress.

entries.title: Trump pauses attacks for 10 days as talks continue
entries.why: The first announced pause of US attacks (on energy plants) during talks.

entries.title: Israel strikes across Iran as US says talks continue
entries.why: Wide Israeli strikes across Iran and Iranian launches.

entries.title: Israel strikes Iran's uranium plant, Tehran vows retaliation

values.countedAs: reported casualties with no stated place or kind; may count Iran's dead only

entries.why: Israeli strikes on a uranium plant, a heavy-water complex and industry: war strikes on nuclear sites (hit since the first week), not nuclear talks.

entries.title: Trump slams NATO as US-Israeli strikes hit Iran
entries.why: The same day's strikes on Iran's nuclear and energy sites and Trump's NATO criticism over the war.

entries.title: Twelve wounded at Saudi air base in Iranian attack
entries.why: An Iranian strike on US forces at a Saudi base; a casualty update.

entries.title: Millions flee after strikes disrupt aid routes
entries.why: Splits its subject between strikes on Iran's health services and Lebanon's displacement (optional in the Lebanon key too).

entries.title: Houthis strike Israel as US Marines arrive
entries.why: Headline is the Houthis' first strikes on Israel (the Houthi front is out), but it frames them as widening the Iran war and gives the US Marine buildup its own strand.

entries.title: Senate fails to limit US role in Iran conflict
entries.why: Another failed war-powers vote: Congress on the war itself.

entries.title: House Democrats demand hearing after US casualties and missile strikes

values.countedAs: civilian deaths with no stated place

entries.why: Congressional oversight of the US campaign, with US and civilian casualty counts.

entries.title: Pakistan offers to host US–Iran talks amid troop buildup
entries.why: Mediation to end the war and fears of a US ground assault.

entries.title: Security Council condemns Iran missile and drone strikes
entries.why: Security Council Resolution 2817 on Iran's strikes on its Gulf neighbors: a formal international response to the war.

entries.title: Trump warns of destroying Iran’s energy infrastructure
entries.why: A threat against Iran's power, oil and water sites with Hormuz as the lever; repeats the earlier power-plant threats (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: Iran strikes tanker near Dubai after Trump threats
entries.why: An attack on a merchant tanker, but off Dubai and "part of multiple missile and drone attacks" amid US threats against Iran's energy sites: split between shipping and the war (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: Diplomacy stalls as strikes and tanker attack disrupt oil flows
entries.why: War diary: US-Israeli strikes, Iranian retaliation and stalled talks; the shipping strand is secondary (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: U.S. and Israel strikes kill supreme leader, spark wider war
entries.why: Longform on the decapitation strike and the widening war, a month after the killing.

entries.title: Vance told Pakistan intermediaries US open to ceasefire, warned strikes
entries.why: US ceasefire signals and strike threats through Pakistan: talks to end the war.

entries.title: US and Israel strike Iran amid heated legal debate
entries.why: Opinion on whether the strikes break the ban on force: about the war's legality, but mainly international law.

entries.title: Trump vows 'extremely hard' strikes as war continues
entries.why: Escalation threats and claims of a crippled Iranian military.

entries.title: Experts warn US strikes threaten Iran's power and water

values.countedAs: deaths in one strike (a girls' school) only
values.quote: Iran says a girls' school strike killed 175

entries.why: Legal experts on US strikes and infrastructure threats, and civilian deaths in Iran.

entries.title: Red Cross: strikes on schools, power may be war crimes

values.countedAs: pupils killed in one missile strike in Minab only
values.quote: a missile strike in Minab killed 175 pupils

entries.why: Civilian harm from the strikes and the Red Cross's war-crimes warning.

entries.title: Iran strikes Amazon facilities in Gulf
entries.why: Iran's strikes on Gulf data centers are part of the war, but the piece is mainly about cloud and AI infrastructure as a target.

entries.title: US vows heavier strikes, threatens bridges and power plants
entries.why: A US threat against Iranian infrastructure (a Hormuz near miss).

entries.title: WHO: over 20 strikes hit Iranian medical sites

values.countedAs: deaths in WHO-verified attacks on health facilities only

entries.why: Humanitarian harm in Iran from the strikes.

entries.title: Pakistan-led bid to bridge US and Tehran stalls
entries.why: Stalled mediation to end the war.

entries.title: Trump and Israel threaten attacks on Iran's energy sites
entries.why: Two US warplanes shot down and an airman missing, the first such loss, with US-Israeli threats against energy sites (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: Iran fires missiles at Israel and Kuwait after Trump threat
entries.why: Iranian retaliation on Israel and a Gulf state, with strikes near Bushehr.

entries.title: Trump sets final deadline, threatens strikes on Iran
entries.why: The ultimatum, infrastructure threats, Iran's proposal to end hostilities and an Israeli strike on South Pars (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: Trump warns of one-night strike as major attacks loom
entries.why: Escalation threats and the rescue of a downed airman inside Iran.

entries.title: US and Iran meet as oil disruption roils markets
entries.why: First story to report the 7 April ceasefire that halted US and Israeli strikes (none published 8-10 April) and the first direct talks; oil is secondary (Hormuz optional, a Lebanon near miss).

entries.title: Major powers flout protections for civilians
entries.why: HRW opinion on the US, Israel and Iran flouting civilian protections in this war; mainly about humanitarian law, and it covers Lebanon too.

entries.title: Trump threatens to destroy Iran’s desalination plants
entries.why: A newsletter roundup whose lead item is the desalination threat; its other items are unrelated.

entries.title: Trump announces two-week ceasefire as Israel bombs Lebanon
entries.why: Analysis of the 7 April ceasefire and its strain, later than the 11 April report; Lebanon is the second strand (Lebanon optional).

entries.title: Trump orders blockade, warns China and Iran
entries.why: Dual fit: mainly the naval blockade of the strait, but the only story to report that the first peace talks failed, with vows of strikes on Iranian infrastructure that "risks blowing up a fragile ceasefire" (a Hormuz must).

entries.title: Mediators pursue ceasefire while Iran nuclear dispute persists
entries.why: Talks to extend the ceasefire; nuclear suspension is a term in talks to end the war (a near miss in both neighbor keys).

entries.title: U.S.-Iran talks progress as oil route stays closed
entries.why: Talks to end the war as the ceasefire nears expiry; control of the strait is one term (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: Ceasefire masks economic ruin and fear of crackdown
entries.why: War damage and ruin inside Iran under the ceasefire, split with fear of domestic repression.

entries.title: US seizes Iranian ship as ceasefire talks falter
entries.why: Dual fit: a Hormuz must (ship seizure, blockade), but half its subject is this war's ceasefire talks faltering and Iran refusing further talks.

entries.title: Trump extends ceasefire while keeping Iranian ports blockaded
entries.why: The ceasefire is extended indefinitely with conditions for talks; the blockade is secondary (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: Islamabad brokered talks halt direct U.S.–Iran fighting
entries.why: Credits the talks with pausing the fighting, but its main subject is why Pakistan mediates.

entries.title: Trump scraps talks as Iran and US remain deadlocked
entries.why: The US cancels envoy visits and the talks to end the war break down under a fragile ceasefire.

entries.title: US–Israeli strikes damage hospitals and medicine factories in Iran

values.countedAs: civilians among the dead in Iran only

entries.why: Deaths and damage inside Iran from the campaign, added up; not a new turn.

entries.title: Trump warns Iran, consults oil firms on months-long export squeeze
entries.why: Mostly the naval squeeze on Iran's oil exports (out), with a war strand of its own: Trump pressing for a deal, Iran threatening retaliation and the war's $25bn cost.

entries.title: White House says Iran hostilities have terminated
entries.why: The US formally tells Congress the hostilities have "terminated" as the 60-day War Powers clock runs out; not an end event, since strikes resume on 10 May.

entries.title: Trump hurt by prolonged Iran war and oil shock
entries.why: Where the war stands after two months: no exit, Iran's offer rejected and renewed strikes weighed.

entries.title: War spikes prices and wipes out millions of jobs
entries.why: Iran's economic collapse, blamed on the war and bombardment but also on sanctions, the naval blockade and the internet shutdown ("Mixed causes reduce attribution"): split with themes that are out.

entries.title: Iran ceasefire follows rapid U.S. arms depletion
entries.why: About US missile stocks, but it recounts how the 40-day war was fought and ties the 7 April ceasefire to interceptor exhaustion.

entries.title: US bypasses Congress, approves $8.6 billion Middle East weapons deal
entries.why: An arms-sales decision justified by the war emergency to restock Israel and the Gulf states, not about the war's course.

entries.title: US and Iran clash over Gulf oil route
entries.why: Dual fit: the fight is over the strait (a Hormuz must), but it is also the first US-Iran exchange of strikes after the 7 April truce, with Iran hitting a UAE oil port.

entries.title: US hits Iranian military sites after attacks
entries.why: US strikes on missile, drone and command sites in Iran after attacks on US forces, which Iran calls a ceasefire violation: strikes on Iranian soil resume during the truce.

entries.title: US rejects Iran peace offer as tensions rise
entries.why: The talks break down when the US publicly rejects Iran's reply; threats from Iran and Israel follow (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: Iran rejects US terms, Hormuz shipping nearly halted
entries.why: Trump calls the ceasefire "on life support" after Tehran rejects US terms; continues the 11 May breakdown, the Hormuz strand secondary (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: House vote leaves Trump free to keep striking Iran
entries.why: A tied House vote on halting US military action against Iran; the third close vote, changing nothing on the ground.

entries.title: Trump says he paused attack, signals possible Iran deal
entries.why: A decision to pause renewed strikes after Iran's peace proposal, with a threat of a full assault if talks fail.

entries.title: UAE's Barakah plant back online after Gulf strike
entries.why: Damage in a Gulf state from a wartime strike, but the story is the restart and our text never names the attacker.

entries.title: Khamenei orders enriched uranium to remain in Iran
entries.why: Khamenei's order hardens Iran's position in the peace talks and "could ... complicate efforts to end the US‑Israeli war on Iran": uranium as a term of the talks to end the war.

entries.title: U.S. says Spain denied base access, questions alliance membership
entries.why: Mainly a US-NATO rift, caused by allies denying base access for the Iran war.

entries.title: US and Iran report progress toward ending Gulf war
entries.why: Talks to end the war on Iran's 14-point proposal; progress, not a deal (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: US strikes hit southern Iran during Qatar peace talks
entries.why: US strikes on missile sites and mine-laying boats in Iran during the Qatar talks; another round of the tit-for-tat begun on 10 May.

entries.title: Trump must approve 60-day US–Iran truce amid strikes
entries.why: Negotiators reach a memorandum on a 60-day truce extension, while strikes on Bandar Abbas and Iranian attacks test it.

entries.title: Arab states restrict US military access after regional strikes
entries.why: Gulf damage and Saudi limits on US basing for the war are a major strand, but the Gulf economic outlook dominates.

entries.title: U.S. strikes Iranian radar after drones threatened shipping
entries.why: US strikes on Iranian coastal radar after drone shoot-downs, complicating the talks; another tit-for-tat round (Hormuz optional).

entries.title: US says missiles intercepted as talks stall
entries.why: Renewed Iranian missile and drone attacks, US strikes on Qeshm and stalled talks; Lebanon is context (a Lebanon near miss).

entries.title: Trump's ceasefires haven't stopped cross-border strikes
entries.why: A roundup of three fraying truces (Gaza, Lebanon, Iran); the US-Iran strikes are one strand (Lebanon optional).

entries.title: US and Iran exchange strikes as missiles cross borders
entries.why: The same exchange as the 6 June radar story, reported a day later.

entries.title: Trump orders strikes after helicopter downing
entries.why: A US Apache is shot down and Trump orders strikes inside Iran just as a deal was reported close.

entries.title: Trump says strikes will resume as sanctions hit Iran networks
entries.why: Trump says strikes will resume amid the exchange after the helicopter downing; sanctions and IAEA figures are secondary.

entries.title: US hits key facilities in Iran during renewed attacks
entries.why: Hegseth confirms repeated strikes on Iranian facilities as pressure for a deal; the round begun on 10 June.

entries.title: Iran strikes hit US allies, raise shipping and oil fears

notes: Provenance: drafted by Claude Opus 5.5 on 2026-11-21 from the local copy of published stories (to 2026-11-18), with an adversarial second pass; the owner accepted it without a person reviewing the entries, near misses or values. Boundary: an entry is a must when the war itself is its main subject: strike rounds, Iran's retaliation on Israel, US forces and the Gulf states, deaths and damage from them, the killing of Iran's leaders, war aims and threats to widen or resume strikes, ceasefires, pauses and their breakdowns, talks and deals to end the war, and decisions by Congress or allies about the war. Nuclear points count when they are terms in the talks to end the war ("mediators-pursue-ceasefire-while-iran-nuclear-dispute-persists", "vance-makes-enrichment-cuts-a-condition-for-ending-war", "tehran-rejects-uranium-concessions-in-ceasefire-talks", "khamenei-orders-enriched-uranium-to-remain-in-iran"); strikes on nuclear sites are war strikes. Optional entries are mainly about something else but give the war a major strand of their own, or split their subject with another front: deals and talks that both end the fighting and reopen Hormuz, regional roundups, arms sales, munitions stocks and force moves justified by the war (the 3 March interceptor stories, the 16 March missile shift, the 3 May arms depletion), outside support for Iran (Russia's drones and intelligence, the October China-Russia piece), legality and humanitarian-law opinions that are not about the strikes' own harm (HRW's piece covers Lebanon too; the legal experts' letter and the Red Cross warning are must, since they report the strikes' civilian harm in Iran), the cyber, internet-blackout and AI-targeting angles, Iran's and the Gulf's wartime economies where sanctions, the blockade or shipping share the blame ("war-spikes-prices-and-wipes-out-millions-of-jobs", "iran-war-leaves-shipping-and-investment-at-risk"), tanker attacks off the Gulf states framed by the war, Pakistan's mediation as foreign policy. Stories mainly about Hormuz shipping, Lebanon, the pre-war standoff, the nuclear program, oil and fuel markets, Yemen and the Houthis, sanctions or the "Iron Gate" land blockade are out; the 15 most tempting are near misses. Start: the US-Israeli strikes of 28 February, first reported on 1 March; February buildup and nuclear-talk stories are out (the 15 February strike plans and the 26 February threats are near misses). Same-event clusters: stories published on one day often share one timestamp (02:15 UTC), so the turning point inside a same-day cluster is a judgment call: 1 March (the launch story over the first toll), 2 March (the Khamenei strike story over the succession analysis), 18 June (the end-the-war story over the two other deal stories), 2 September ("us-hits-irgc-targets-iran-vows-heavy-retaliation" over "trump-warns-of-largest-strike-as-us-bombs-iran") and 17-18 November (the Bahrain drone story over the Qeshm strike story); another story of the same cluster is an equally valid turning point. Later same-event stories are routine (the opening strikes, Khamenei's succession, the frigate Dena, the 22 March power-plant ultimatum, the 7 April ceasefire, the 6-7 June and 10-12 June rounds, the July resumption, the late-July pause). Stories that only repeat an earlier first are routine: the 28 March uranium-plant strike (nuclear sites were struck from the first week), the 16 March rejection of mediation (Trump refused talks on 9 March) and the 13 July strikes on Qatar and the UAE (Gulf states hit since 2 March, US bases in the Gulf two days earlier). No stories were published 8-10 April, so the 11 April story is the first to report the 7 April ceasefire. 8 July (strikes resume) and 9 July (Trump declares the ceasefire over) are kept as two turning points. No story reports the August ceasefire that a 29 August story says "eased the worst fighting"; the 2 September strikes are marked as the resumption. Numbers: deaths in Iran are not a clean series across sources: at least 201 (1 March), at least 555 "in Iran" (5 March, below the 787 of 4 March, likely an older tally), at least 1,230 (6 and 8 March), over 1,300 by Iran's claim (18 March), HRANA's 3,000-plus (20 March) against "more than 2,000 people in Iran" two days later, and at least 3,636 (29 April), the last cumulative Iran toll; later stories give only round or strike counts. War tolls with no stated place (over 1,250, about 2,000, over 2,000, over 1,900 casualties, more than 7,000), civilian-only counts and every count for one strike or one strike round are recorded as values that do not match: the Minab school (at least 51, 180, more than 168, 175 twice, about 150 in the UN's later finding, more than 150), Isfahan (at least 15), WHO-verified attacks on health facilities (at least nine), and the 14 and 2 of July strikes. US service members killed: 6 (5 and 6 March), 8 (11 March), 13 (30 March), at least 17 (20 July), 18 (23 July). Not tracked: US wounded (at least 150 on 11 March, more than 300 on 28 March but 290 on 30 March, about 500 on 23 July), the Minab school toll as a figure of its own (its counts are non-matching values of deaths in Iran), deaths in Israel and the Gulf states (stated per incident only) and target counts. Dual fits: 18 stories are must entries of hormuz-shipping-2026. The 7 that lead on the war itself, its fighting or its end, are must entries here too, and the linking eval counts a must of two keys as rightly joined in either development's overview (the owner's call, 2026-11-21): "us-and-iran-clash-over-gulf-oil-route", "us-and-iran-agree-to-end-war-and-reopen-hormuz", "ceasefire-ends-strikes-and-reopens-key-shipping-lane", "u-s-and-iran-agree-60-day-roadmap-open-shipping-lane", "us-and-iran-pause-strikes-and-agree-to-doha-talks", "us-strikes-iran-after-hormuz-blockade-us-bases-targeted-abroad" and "us-strikes-iran-as-shipping-falls-by-90". The 11 that lead on the strait are optional here: "us-seizes-iranian-ship-as-ceasefire-talks-falter", "trump-orders-blockade-warns-china-and-iran" (the only story to report that the first direct peace talks failed), "us-iran-reach-provisional-deal-to-reopen-strait-of-hormuz", "us-and-iran-clash-over-strait-tolls-and-inspections", "iran-and-us-clash-over-shipping-rules-sparking-strikes", "us-and-iran-weigh-reopening-a-key-oil-route", "iran-offers-seven-day-plan-to-reopen-shipping", "trump-rejects-iran-s-plan-to-reopen-vital-oil-route", "iran-says-us-offer-fails-to-reopen-key-sea-route", "iran-threatens-us-bases-as-tankers-burn" and "washington-used-pause-to-secure-oil-shipping-lanes". "iran-strikes-tanker-near-dubai-after-trump-threats" is optional in both keys. Stories that are near misses or optional in a neighbor key and must here (e.g. "trump-says-iran-campaign-very-soon-as-oil-tops-100", "iran-strikes-tel-aviv-with-cluster-missiles", "trump-threatens-to-obliterate-iran-power-plants") are consistent with those keys. Open on 16 November 2026: every truce in our stories was broken by later strikes (the 7 April ceasefire by 10 May, the 29 May memorandum by the 6-12 June rounds, the 18 June deal by the 27 June strikes and Trump's 9 July declaration, the 30 June and 27 July pauses by 8 and 30 July, the August ceasefire by 2 September). Trump's 10 November statement that the fighting is "effectively over" comes with no ceasefire or deal and with US forces ready to resume attacks, and the talks are shelved on 13 November: no end event by 16 November. The open call rests on that evidence alone; the 17-18 November stories (Iranian drones at a US base in Bahrain, the US strike on Qeshm) postdate 16 November, are entries, and only confirm it. "trump-pulls-vance-from-iran-negotiations" is published as "Vance shifted from Iran diplomacy to domestic issues".
